Being pregnant with a 2 year old I wanted local walking distance convenience and good service for my children more than anything. I called Monday and was offered an appt for my 2 year old, in a months time! Baring in mind I said he is having an allergy to something. They then offered me an appt the end of the week but elsewhere and explain they use iHUB and send pts mostly elsewhere because they are always fully booked for the month (so the receptionist says). This defeats the whole purpose of joining this surgery when I have to travel further out than I need to and also I have never ever not been given an appt on the same day by a GP or at least spoken to on the phone for me let alone a 2 year old toddler. Highly considering changing my sons GP after this experience because getting an appt promptly is so important and most GPs offer now so this is truly ridiculous! Even my local Pharmacy were shocked when I told them and replied ‘but he’s a child!’. They even recommended another local GP surgery which they have heard great things about which says a lot. I’m basically writing this review to give a heads up that if distance and prompt appts are your priority, maybe consider elsewhere.

Update:- after attending an appt today and my first time visiting the practice, I just want to add every single Dr there seemed brilliant, especially the one who tended to our son. The practice manager also kindly gave us her time to hear our complaint about one of the admin members on the phone who spoke to us unprofessionally. They reassured me they can see us sooner and even on same day if absolutely necessary. I feel much better after leaving this appt and will see how it goes. Thank you for taking the time to share your experience, and we are truly sorry for the frustration and concern this situation has caused—especially given that you are pregnant and caring for a young child.

We completely understand how important it is to have quick and convenient access to care, particularly for children. Our usual waiting time for routine GP appointments is around two weeks, but over the past month we have experienced an unusually high level of demand, which has unfortunately pushed our waiting times up further. We are actively working to bring this back down, including bringing in additional clinical staff.

For urgent concerns, we do have a duty doctor (often two) available each day from 08:30 to 18:30. If your child needs to be assessed more urgently, please do call and ask to speak to the on-call doctor, who can review the situation and arrange appropriate care. We are very sorry if this option was not clearly explained to you at the time.

In terms of iHUB, this is a service funded by local GP practices to help support patient care during periods of high demand. While we appreciate it may not always be as convenient as being seen at your registered practice, it is intended to ensure patients can still access timely appointments when we are particularly busy. 

We are really sorry that your experience did not reflect the level of care we aim to provide, and we genuinely appreciate you bringing this to our attention.

Best wishes,

Dr. James Hibberd

Unfortunately, referrals that do not meet these criteria are often rejected by the specialist service and returned to the GP practice, which can delay care further and cause additional frustration for patients.

Our GPs are required to follow these guidelines and to ensure that all appropriate assessments, investigations, and initial management steps have been completed before making a referral. This is not a reflection of the seriousness of a patient’s symptoms, but rather a necessary part of ensuring referrals are accepted and that patients receive the most appropriate care as efficiently as possible.

We strongly encourage you to book a further appointment with one of our clinicians to review your symptoms, discuss any changes or progression, and explore the next appropriate steps in your care. If you would prefer, you can also ask about seeking a second opinion within the practice.

Dr. James Hibberd
